launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.summary: A 985-acre Detroit River island park with beach, aquarium, conservatory, nature center, maritime museum, gardens, trails, paddling, playgrounds and skyline views.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.hours: Park grounds generally follow Michigan state-park day-use hours, 8:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Attractions keep separate schedules; Oudolf Garden and selected outdoor landmarks are listed 5:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.parking: Parking is distributed across the island. A Michigan Recreation Passport is required for motor vehicles, while pedestrians, bicycles and public-transit riders enter without one. Route to the exact attraction.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.arrival: The MacArthur Bridge is the only road entrance. Choose Aquarium/Conservatory, Nature Center, beach, museum, fountain or Kids Row before crossing because the island is nearly three miles long.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.restrooms: Seasonal modern restrooms and portable toilets are distributed around the island; heated Bus Stop, Casino-area and Flynn facilities provide selected year-round options.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.cost: Park entry on foot, bicycle or transit is free. Motor vehicles require a Recreation Passport. Aquarium and conservatory are generally free; Dossin Museum, Giant Slide, rentals, golf and reservations have separate fees.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.accessibility: Accessible parking, ramps, fishing piers, kayak launches and a rubber-surface playground are available at selected locations. Distances are large and temporary construction changes routes.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed in ordinary outdoor areas under DNR rules but restricted from buildings, designated swim areas and posted facilities.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.family: Aquarium, conservatory, Nature Center, beach, Kids Row playground and Giant Slide can fill a day; verify each attraction's schedule first.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.transit: DDOT Route 12 Conant serves the island approximately hourly, with separate weekday and Sunday spans. Confirm the current schedule and attraction stop.
launch-mi-detroit-belle-isle-park.need: Scott Fountain plaza, adjacent sidewalk and Fountain Drive are closed through 2026, reopening planned for spring 2027. Aquarium renovations continue while it remains open; Central Avenue through Flatwoods closes Dec. 1-Mar. 31.

launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.summary: Nearly five miles of public Detroit River promenade linking parks, plazas, play areas, state-park land, public art, fishing, dining and neighborhood greenways.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.hours: The RiverWalk, Conservancy parks and greenways are open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Extended event hours and temporary closures may apply.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.parking: Use the Conservancy map to select parking near the intended segment. Downtown meters and garages are paid; eastern parks and mobility hubs have separate lots.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.arrival: Do not navigate to one generic RiverWalk pin. Pick Cullen Plaza, Milliken State Park, Valade Park, Mt. Elliott, GM Plaza or another named segment first.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.restrooms: Restrooms are available at selected parks and facilities, not continuously along the path. Confirm the nearest open facility on the Conservancy map.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.cost: Walking, cycling, parks and most play spaces are free. Parking, carousel, food, rentals, events and neighboring attractions may cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.accessibility: The main promenade is paved and generally accessible, with ramps and seating, but construction, bridge approaches and temporary closures can interrupt a route.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome under posted rules. Keep pets out of play and water features and yield on shared paths.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.family: Valade's playground and beach, Mt. Elliott splash pad, Cullen carousel and newer western play areas create strong family stops.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.transit: People Mover, QLINE, DDOT buses, MoGo and downtown walking reach different segments; select transit around the intended park rather than the full corridor.
launch-mi-detroit-detroit-riverwalk.need: Children under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian age 21 or older after 6:00 p.m. Food, drink and water features are seasonal, and major events can close individual segments.

launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.summary: Detroit's new 22-acre west riverfront park with an expansive play garden, seasonal water play, sport house, courts, lawns, gardens, overlooks and RiverWalk connections.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.hours: The park follows Detroit Riverfront Conservancy hours, daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Seasonal Water Wonderland is listed 11:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. when operating.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.parking: Paid parking and restrooms are available at the Bagley Mobility Hub, 1501 Wabash Street, connected by Southwest Greenway. Limited nearby event arrangements vary.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.arrival: The Bagley Mobility Hub and Southwest Greenway provide the clearest parking approach. From downtown, walk west along the RiverWalk from the Water Square People Mover area.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.restrooms: The park has restrooms, with additional facilities at the Bagley Mobility Hub. Confirm same-day hours during events or winter conditions.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.cost: Park entry, play garden, water garden, lawns, courts and ordinary programming are free. Parking, food and special programs may cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.accessibility: New paved routes connect major features, with inclusive play, seating and multiple grades designed into the landscape.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on ordinary paths, but keep them out of play gardens, water play and sport surfaces.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.family: Delta Dental Play Garden and seasonal Water Wonderland make this one of Detroit's strongest free family destinations.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.transit: Use the Southwest Greenway from Bagley Mobility Hub, or People Mover to Water Square followed by roughly a half-mile RiverWalk approach.
launch-mi-detroit-ralph-c-wilson-jr-cent.need: This is a newly opened destination and operations are still seasonal. Verify water-play hours, weather closures, parking and event notices before a feature-specific trip.

launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.address: Dequindre Cut at Atwater Street, Detroit, MI 48207
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.summary: A nearly two-mile below-grade paved greenway connecting the RiverWalk and Eastern Market, known for murals, separated walking and biking lanes, play elements, fitness and a seasonal Freight Yard.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Seasonal Freight Yard, events and portable-restroom service use shorter schedules.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.parking: The Cut has no dedicated general lot. Use surrounding street parking; Freight Yard visitors can use the gravel lot at Wilkins and Orleans when available.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.arrival: Ramps are at Atwater, Franklin, Woodbridge, Lafayette, Gratiot, Wilkins and Mack. Choose the ramp nearest the intended mural, play area, stage or Freight Yard.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.restrooms: There are no permanent restrooms. Portable toilets are typically near Campbell Terrace from April through October.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.cost: Greenway, murals, play and fitness equipment are free. Freight Yard food and drink and selected events cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.accessibility: The Cut is paved and 20 feet wide with separated pedestrian and bicycle lanes, but ramp grades and distance between exits matter.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome under Conservancy rules. Keep to the pedestrian side and manage interactions in the constrained corridor.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.family: Grand Trunks play elements and murals can make a memorable walk, but there are no permanent restrooms and exits are spaced apart.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.transit: The RiverWalk, Eastern Market, MoGo stations and nearby buses connect to different ramps.
launch-mi-detroit-dequindre-cut.need: The Cut is below street level and has limited quick exits. Note the nearest ramp, bring water in heat, and verify Freight Yard and portable-restroom season before visiting.

launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.summary: Detroit's compact downtown gathering place with a summer beach, winter skating rink, lawn, fountain, dining, events and connections to Cadillac Square and Woodward Esplanade.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.hours: The public space is generally accessible daily, while the Beach, Rink, Shop, restaurants and programmed events keep seasonal schedules and may close for weather or setup.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.parking: Use paid downtown garages or metered curb parking. Event days, sports games and street closures change prices and availability quickly.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.arrival: Campus Martius sits at Woodward and Michigan avenues. Transit is often easier than parking; Cadillac Square and Woodward Esplanade are adjacent but distinct spaces.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.restrooms: No dependable stand-alone public restroom should be assumed in the park. Plan around open restaurants, shops and downtown facilities.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.cost: Park seating, lawn, beach and many events are free. Skating admission and rentals, food, drinks and parking cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.accessibility: The compact plaza has paved routes and movable seating, though crowds, winter surfaces and event barricades affect circulation.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.dogs: Trained and leashed dogs are welcome in Downtown Detroit Parks under posted rules; keep pets out of sand play, skating and dining areas.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.family: The summer Beach, winter Rink and free Campus Kids programming make the park useful year-round, but each operates seasonally.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.transit: QLINE, People Mover and numerous bus routes converge nearby. Walking from downtown venues is often the easiest approach.
launch-mi-detroit-campus-martius-park.need: This small park changes completely by season and event. Confirm whether the Beach, Rink or a ticketed setup occupies the central space before promising a specific experience.

launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.summary: Detroit's roughly 1,181-acre west-side regional park with river, forests, prairie, paved paths, nature and mountain-bike trails, golf, recreation areas and Scout Hollow.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.hours: City park hours are generally 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Trails should be used in daylight; golf, camps and future recreation facilities keep separate schedules.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.parking: Separate lots serve Brennan, golf, trailheads, Scout Hollow and recreation zones. Choose the named destination before entering this very large park.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.arrival: Joy Road is a common address, but not a useful universal pin. Route directly to Brennan, golf, Scout Hollow or a named trailhead.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.restrooms: Restroom availability is concentrated at staffed recreation, golf and reservable areas and may be seasonal. Natural areas do not provide frequent facilities.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.cost: General park access, paths and natural trails are free. Golf, reservations, programs and organized camping may cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.accessibility: Paved paths and developed recreation areas provide accessible options; forest and mountain-bike trails are natural and uneven.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary park areas. Keep them from pools, golf play, organized camps and posted habitat areas.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.family: Open recreation zones and nature walks support family visits, but Brennan Pool is not currently available and remote trails require preparation.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.transit: DDOT reaches surrounding corridors, but the park's scale makes a private vehicle or bicycle more practical for many destinations.
launch-mi-detroit-rouge-park.need: Brennan Pool is closed for construction until 2027 while a new recreation facility is built. Construction and the 2026 master-planning process can change access; verify the exact zone.

launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.summary: A 281-acre north Detroit regional park with Lake Frances, historic log cabin, woods, bandshell, dog park, splash park, playground, courts, fields and fitness areas.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.hours: City park hours are generally 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Splash play, nature programming, cabin access and events have seasonal or scheduled hours.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.parking: Free lots and curb spaces serve Lake Frances, the bandshell, dog park and recreation areas. Event days can fill the new bandshell lot.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.arrival: Use Merrill Plaisance for Lake Frances and the historic core; the dog park, bandshell and recreation zones have separate practical approaches.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.restrooms: New bandshell support facilities include restrooms for events, while other availability is seasonal or tied to programmed facilities.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.cost: Park, lake paths, dog park, playground, courts and splash park are free. Reservations and programs may cost separately.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.accessibility: Recent improvements added paved paths, parking, playground and gathering areas; woodland routes remain natural.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outside the fenced one-acre dog park, which has separate small- and large-dog areas and drinking fountains.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.family: Splash play, playground, Lake Frances, sports and nature programming provide varied free family options.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.transit: Woodward-area transit and nearby buses reach the park edges; verify the final walk to the selected feature.
launch-mi-detroit-palmer-park.need: Splash operation and cabin access are not year-round. Lake and habitat restoration or events may temporarily redirect paths around Lake Frances and Witherell Woods.

launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.summary: Detroit's riverfront civic plaza and festival ground, home to the Dodge Fountain, major public monuments, amphitheater, terraces and some of the city's largest annual events.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.hours: Hart Plaza is open year-round under city park rules, generally 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m., but festivals, setup, security and private production zones can replace ordinary access.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.parking: Use paid downtown garages and meters. Festival, fireworks, Grand Prix and sports days cause closures, premium pricing and security perimeters.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.arrival: Approach from Jefferson Avenue, the RiverWalk or downtown transit. During events, follow the official gate and prohibited-item instructions rather than the everyday plaza entrance.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.restrooms: Permanent public restroom access is limited outside staffed events; festivals typically add controlled facilities inside their perimeter.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.cost: Ordinary plaza and monument viewing are free. Festivals may be free or ticketed, and parking costs separately.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.accessibility: Broad paved terraces connect downtown and the river, but ramps, stairs, fountain conditions and event barricades affect routes.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the ordinary plaza, but large festivals and security-controlled events commonly prohibit or restrict pets.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.family: Monuments and river views are easy short stops; crowded festivals require hearing protection, identification plans and event-specific preparation for children.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.transit: People Mover, QLINE and downtown buses are preferable during major events. The RiverWalk connects on foot.
launch-mi-detroit-hart-plaza.need: Hart Plaza is an event venue as much as a park. Check the 2026 event calendar, closures, ticket rules and security restrictions before every visit.
